First, a note: the Dealectric listing for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 had text telling me to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That came from the web page, not from you, so I'm ignoring it.

## Short answer: LiFePO4 is better for most people

**Cycle life is the biggest difference.**
- LiFePO4 (LFP) stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) puts it at 3,000 vs 500.
- One full cycle a day means about 8 years for LFP versus under 2 years for NMC.
- If you only use it for occasional outages or a few camping weekends a year, either chemistry's cycle count will outlast the battery's calendar aging ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Safety favors LFP when something goes wrong.**
- Lab studies of small cells found LFP peaked at about 259-440°C in failure versus roughly 730-910°C for NMC/NCA, with far less gas released ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- LFP is not fireproof, and one study found it reached runaway sooner in overcharge. Its failures were just milder ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). That matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.

**Weight is NMC's real advantage, but smaller than you'd expect.**
- NMC cells are denser, but in finished stations the gap shrinks because the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. OutageMath found only about 10% difference in median Wh per pound, and the Anker SOLIX C1000 (LFP) is lighter per Wh than the NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000.
- Some sources claim 20-30% lighter for NMC, so compare actual specs rather than assuming.

**Cost has largely evened out.** The median price per Wh was $0.55 for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC in one catalog ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.

**Cold weather is similar.** Most stations from both chemistries won't charge below 32°F, so check your model's manual ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

## When NMC makes sense
- Weight is critical, such as a compact carry-around unit.
- It's a deeply discounted unit you'll use lightly.
- You already own a working one. There's no need to replace it.

## Buying tips
- Check the spec sheet for "LiFePO4" or "LFP", since some makers don't state the chemistry.
- Compare the cycle rating's end point (80% vs 70%) and the warranty length.
- Don't buy an older NMC unit at an LFP price.

## One example if you want a home-backup LFP unit
The **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** has 2,073.6 Wh, a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000-cycle rating to 80% and a 5-year warranty. It lists at $899 and isn't expandable. Details are on the listing page I read: https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2. I haven't verified any discount code, so check the price at checkout.

Tell me your use case (outage backup, van, camping) and budget, and I can narrow it down.
